posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
My Story:

 

Get E-mail saying beautiful cards will arrive on Friday.  The world looks bright and hope swells for the future.

Worry sets in, how will I protect my beautiful cards?

Order great sleeves, Amazon Prime says "don't worry they will arrive with your cards", the world is in harmony and beautiful.

Thursday. . .  Get E-Mail from Fed Ex:  "Where do you even live bro, this address is crap, what is a Pennsylvania?  We're sending this back to St Louis and we hope you die."  (actual E-mail text)

The world sinks into despair and weeping.  Why would we even try to stop OblivAeon, bring on the void, there's no point to this life anyway.

Friday:  Drop kids at school.  Lose to OblivAeon.  Post on Forums.  Put on shoes, walk out door and see two boxes on the porch.  One from Amazon, one from GtG.

Walk inside, post this message, and leave late to pick up kids.

posts.name: NinjaMonkey
posts.cooked:
The new cards are gorgeous. Love them.

As for some foilers:

We all say it (most of us at least), if you are dealing damage with Argent Adept, Visionary, or Captain Cosmic you are doing something wrong. Looks like GtG said "challenge accepted".

The Harpy looks interesting, but I'm really hoping she brings something to the table that really synergizes with the rest of the Dark Watch team. Maybe some out of turn power uses to make Expat's Aim a little more attractive option. Or maybe ways to feed Nightmist more cards. Something. I love the Dark Watch team as a concept. In play at the moment they just feel like a group of individuals who just happen to be fighting the same villain.

The new Xtreme Prime Wardens: WOW, just WOW.

The Freedom V: I haven't had time to really dig into how their new powers will work together but they all look pretty interesting. Oh, and if you thought Freedom V Legacy's power was broken, wait until you read the incap abilities.

Decks I Must Have Yesterday: The Idealist and Akash'Thriya. I don't know what kind of crazy mechanics GtG has going on for these 2 but I really wanna get into those decks and see what the heck is going on.

Biggest surprise: Stuntman. This is the character I was least looking forward to. After seeing his power though, I'm really interested to see what is in his deck. It's not that his power is game breaking or anything. Its just hints at a different play style.

Biggest disappointment: Benchmark. I was really looking forward to him. His power though doesn't really tell me much about him or draw me in. I still hold out hope his deck will be awesome though.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Spoiler Time:

Sleeving my cards and saying things.

 

At the meet and greet Adam was asked what was happening on several of the incaps.  One that stood out to me was Scholar of the infinite.

Scholar and Guise are fading out, Scholar is pushing the Philosopher stone into Guise to save him.  (The next sentence is my understanding, but not expressly stated) Scholar does not survive this, and somehow the Stone merges with Guise.

If anyone is curious, the FV set of incaps do indeed tell the story of the FV fighting OblivAeon, they go together, although not necessarily direct line.

Lifeline's incap is the saddest art in the game, according to Adam.  When I stated that Bloogo could pull through, Christopher laughed and said, "Sure, he's fine, Bloogo just went to the farm."

Adept's Dark Dynamics features one of the Virtuoso's instruments.  It is a dark instrument and thus the incap.  (It's a conductor's baton with a rose wrapped around it)

Xtreme Prime Warden (XPW) Adept's incap may also feature a virtuoso instrument.

Prime Warden Cosmic is fixed!  seriously, play that variant now.  (no longer prevents the destuction)

I'm listening to "Can I Play with Madness" on you tube right now, because the video fits that incap so very well (XPW Cosmic).

I don't understand Prime Warden Haka's incap, he rules in the arena.  Must have been really bad card luck.

When it comes to the XPW cards, I can tell you that there was a battle between Balance and Awesome, and Awesome won.

Redeemer Fanatic's incap is my favorite art in the entire game.  So much for playing nice.

Beardy Ra incap:  "I'm sorry, that is clearly a mane and not a neckbeard.  I take it back."

Naturalist Desperate Prey incap:  You know Akash photoshopped that to make it look like she's leaning on the mountain, right?

There are a ton of references and jokes in Adam's art, one of his favorite jokes is Idealist's incap.

Luminary's incap is one of my favorite pieces of storytelling in the game.

Heroic Luminary's incap Legacy has the greatest expression.  (Heroic Luminary is officially what Adam and Christopher call her unofficially)

Tachyon's body language in Harpy's incap. . . wow.

Professor Polution, meet Akash'thriya.  (I can't imagine that goes well)

Stuntman (Tireur Incroyable) incap I can confirm that Ambuscade has those scars in the RPG, Adam didn't know about Tactics.

Benchmark's suit isn't just made by RevoCorp, it is Revenant's suit.  Also there have apparently been more than one pilot of the revenant suit.  Revenant is the head of Revo-Corp.  That should help explain his incap.

Bonus points to anyone who can figure out the 4 people on the back of Benchmark's supply and demand card.

Hmm. . . I wonder why that wrecking ball on Malpractice's incap is all foil?  what could that mean?

Greazer so glad to be able to target a Sentinel.

Super Sentai Idealist is the best card ever.  Both sides.

Guise's third incap, the funky dance is not optional.

Completionist Guise gets a bonus if his card is sleeved.  I don't know what it is, but that is official.

 

Last, but definitely not least, they do fit in the box sleeved.  Rather perfectly I might add.

Chaosmancer:
  • Who is the blue spectral lady on Unleashed Visionary's incap. She doesn't look like any other figure I remember seeing. 
  • Black Spot Commodora and Void Akash'thriya, anyone lse wondering if those purple energy forms are connected somehow? Is that how the Capitan removed the Black Spot and ended up a villain again, she merged with Akash'thriya and the two of them were one for a short time?

I have a theory on that blue lady! Not enough to make a footenotes post out of it, but whens the last time I got to post a story theory? I'll enjoy this. 

At the moment, there are quite a few instances of art where we see characters depicted in this "spectral" form. Visionary and Dark Visionary are in the majority of them as early as base Visionary's original incap art. But there have been other's as well. Remember the incap art for Citizen Hammer in VotM? There is even a point where we see Argent Adept depicted in this spectral form (though I forget wich card it's on off the top of my head). So I found myself asking…myself…is there anything that could possibly tie Visionary, Dark Visionary, and Argent Adept of all characters, together? And you know what? There is.

THE VOID

The Void isn't just based around an upcoming environment (Nexus of the Void), it's been around in game lore for years now, but no ones really known to ask. Argent Adept, as you all know, is the Virtuoso of the Void. He harnesses Void energy as his power source (as per the art Q&As). Whats interesting to me is that, also from the art Q&As, we learned that Dark Visionary also partially resides in the Void as well. Whether it's a natural domain or just someplace where her mind dwells after being ejected from our Vanasas mind is unclear, but we know there is a strong connection between Dark Visionary and the Void. If the Q&A doesn't convince you, maybe the fact that both Argent and DVis both project green energy will?

Either way, I think the basis of this theory boils down into something fairly simple. When we see characters portrayed in this spectral style, we are seeing them inside of the Void, or at least seeing a sort of astral projection into the Void. There is a lot of basis for this from standard comics where mental battles between psychics sometimes take place in other planes of existence (this happens frequently in X-Men titles for instance), and I see a similar thing happening here. The blue lady is likely a being of the Void. Unfortunatly, not much else is known about who or what it is aside from that.

 

On to the Black Spot. I believe I asked this question during the art Q&As if the black circle spot energies between these two characters were the same. I also believe the answer I got was "no". There is a ton of great story we don't know about each of the variants, so it's worth keeping an ear open for and maybe Christopher will dive into these stories in the future.

Visionary and Dark Visionary are in the majority of them as early as base Visionary's original incap art. But there have been other's as well. Remember the incap art for Citizen Hammer in VotM? There is even a point where we see Argent Adept depicted in this spectral form (though I forget wich card it's on off the top of my head). So I found myself asking...myself...is there anything that could possibly tie Visionary, Dark Visionary, and Argent Adept of all characters, together? And you know what? There is.THE VOIDThe Void isn't just based around an upcoming environment (Nexus of the Void), it's been around in game lore for years now, but no ones really known to ask. Argent Adept, as you all know, is the Virtuoso of the Void. He harnesses Void energy as his power source (as per the art Q&As). Whats interesting to me is that, also from the art Q&As, we learned that Dark Visionary also partially resides in the Void as well. Whether it's a natural domain or just someplace where her mind dwells after being ejected from our Vanasas mind is unclear, but we know there is a strong connection between Dark Visionary and the Void. If the Q&A doesn't convince you, maybe the fact that both Argent and DVis both project green energy will?Either way, I think the basis of this theory boils down into something fairly simple. When we see characters portrayed in this spectral style, we are seeing them inside of the Void, or at least seeing a sort of astral projection into the Void. There is a lot of basis for this from standard comics where mental battles between psychics sometimes take place in other planes of existence (this happens frequently in X-Men titles for instance), and I see a similar thing happening here. The blue lady is likely a being of the Void. Unfortunatly, not much else is known about who or what it is aside from that. On to the Black Spot. I believe I asked this question during the art Q&As if the black circle spot energies between these two characters were the same. I also believe the answer I got was "no". There is a ton of great story we don't know about each of the variants, so it's worth keeping an ear open for and maybe Christopher will dive into these stories in the future.

 

I agree with most of your assertions, and I'm also remembering something from the Mission Deck that is interesting.

 

However, she may not be a natural denizen of the Void. She's using a spear and looks human, much like Visionary typically looks human. I find it more likely she is another astral projection into the void, or someone who got trapped there.

 

Or, from her blank expression maybe she a guardian entity, like an AI or spell that was left to guard something… Atlantean?
